$comment: Names the team chose over upstream's, applied after the model and compat rules. `paths` rewrites every path segment containing `from`. `omit` drops upstream files the kit does not ship, such as `make-bot-ui`, which builds pages for the upstream editor's Grok Bot. `rules` rewrite text the same way model-map.json rules do: literal, scoped by upstream path glob, with an exact count. `forbidden` fails the sync if a vendored file still contains the pattern, apart from LICENSE files (whose copyright lines the license requires), the listed words, and the listed per-file exceptions. Faker is the League of Legends player; the mode and its agent carry his name on this team. The upstream editor's name is kept out of the kit.

## automations

pstack also ships a dormant [benny automation pack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack/automations/benny). benny triages slack issue reports, then reproduces and fixes confirmed bugs with real ui evidence. its files are not registered as slash skills.

to set it up, point cursor at [`FOR_AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/blob/main/pstack/automations/benny/FOR_AGENTS.md). setup copies the pack into the target repository at `.cursor/automations/benny/`, enables pstack there for shared skills, and keeps user configuration outside the copied pack. benny runs on cursor automations, so it is cursor-only.

## Build a bot UI with `/make-bot-ui`

One situational skill is for Grok Bot users. [`/make-bot-ui`](../../skills/make-bot-ui/SKILL.md) builds a small page whose buttons wake a bot over a webhook routine. For example, you could swipe through a review queue and have each swipe ask the bot to act on that item. A server on your machine holds the webhook's sender key, so the key never reaches the browser or the chat. The skill also covers exposing the page on Tailscale.
